A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOSAIC and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably across the 27-page v2 and 28-page v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations, a 204-participant human validation study, moderation comparisons, and analyses of engagement, network structure, and agent reasoning.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds GPT-4o-based analysis of emotional salience in true and false news.

M1.justification: The simulation procedure, persona construction, memory system, moderation mechanisms, and operational prompts are retained. The prompts move from Appendix L to M; the new emotional-salience analysis does not modify MOSAIC.

E1.justification: The English true/false-news coverage, human participant population, moderation scenarios, and popularity study remain unchanged. Appendix L characterizes the existing news coverage without adding a new simulated domain or interaction scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same unmoderated, community, third-party, and hybrid comparisons across DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4o, and Claude-3.7-Sonnet, including the same GPT-4o third-party variants. GPT-4o's new annotation role is not an added comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix L introduces a separate balanced analysis of 1,353 real and 1,353 false articles, using GPT-4o ratings across six 1–10 dimensions and high-score proportions. This sampling and scoring protocol applies to the new analysis; the existing human-study and simulation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused dataset diagnostic testing whether false news exhibits emotional features associated with rumor propagation. The existing moderation ablations, demographic comparisons, network/popularity analyses, and agent-reasoning analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The t-tests, chi-square/Cramer's V, and ANOVA reporting are retained. The new tables provide descriptive means, percentage differences, and proportions, without adding repeated-run information, seeds, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Tables 5–6 report emotional intensity of 5.0 for real news versus 7.7 for false news, and high-rumor-potential proportions of 12.9% versus 96.8%, among other results. Tables 1–4 and all existing plotted results are unchanged; the new 7.5x ratio concerns high-rating proportions.

T1.justification: The graph, centrality, clustering, and memory relevance/decay definitions are mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central claims about simulation fidelity, moderation benefits, misinformation propagation, concentrated engagement, and reasoning–behavior misalignment.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies external validity because feeds use recency and follow relationships, and cautions that safety-aligned agents do not establish real human susceptibility. Appendix L additionally interprets its emotional ratings as supporting dataset and simulation realism.

D1.justification: The code pointer changes from an anonymous submission repository to the author-named MOSAIC repository, and Appendix L identifies GPT-4o as its annotator. New consent/data-handling assurances include aggregate-only demographic use, which conflicts with the retained participant-specific persona construction in Section 2.2 and Appendix B. Existing implementation settings and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Five references are added to support the emotional-salience analysis: Berger and Milkman, Chuai and Zhao, Mang et al., Song et al., and Zhang et al. The broader positioning relative to social simulations, fact-checking, and governance research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammar, spelling, and terminology edits throughout, adds an Ethical Considerations section, and inserts the emotional-salience appendix before the renumbered prompts. The existing narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds two tables displaying emotional ratings and high-score distributions. All 14 existing figure graphics and the structures of Tables 1–4 are retained, with some appendix figures and surrounding text shifting through reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency through explicit limits on real-world applicability and additional descriptive evidence about the news corpus. The gain is limited: annotation reliability is unreported, the 7.5x wording concerns high ratings rather than observed virality, and the new aggregate-only data-use assurance conflicts with individualized persona construction. These additions do not substantially strengthen validation of the retained core findings.
